question: Assume today is 2026-08-29. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total freight carried by Canadian railways in July 2026, in tonnes, as it will be first reported by Statistics Canada in its monthly Railway carloadings release (total traffic carried, Canada).

target.what: Total freight carried by Canadian railways (all traffic carried, Canada), as reported in Statistics Canada's monthly Railway carloadings release (Table 23-10-0218-01 / The Daily 'Railway carloadings'), measured in metric tonnes for the month of July 2026
target.caveats: Working interpretation: 'total traffic carried' = total tonnage originated/loaded by Canadian railways in the month (all commodities, domestic plus international/transborder traffic as defined by StatCan's carloadings survey), not revenue ton-km and not just domestic. candidates.data_to_find: Monthly total tonnes carried, Canada, all commodities, from Table 23-10-0218-01 (or The Daily releases) for 2023-2026 through the latest month published before 2026-08-29 (likely June 2026). Also July values for 2023, 2024, 2025 to compute July/June and July/annual seasonal ratios.

methods.rationale: Anchors on the most recent observed July total (p1, 30.7 Mt) and applies a YoY change factor informed by CN weekly carloads/RTM (p149, p150), AAR Canadian carloads (p190), and the flat 2025 annual trend (p44). Shared dependency: p1 is the same StatCan survey as the target; the change factor is the main uncertainty. Failure mode: a large grain or potash swing or a wildfire-driven closure not captured by the factor.

assumptions.name: July 2026 vs July 2025 total tonnage change factor
assumptions.rationale: July 2025 total was 30.7 Mt (p1), slightly above the five-year July average of 29.8 Mt (p2). 2025 annual was roughly flat (-0.2%, p44) and early-2026 months were mixed (Feb 2026 +9.8% YoY, p250). CN late-July 2026 carloads were -4.1% YoY (p149) and RTMs -2.3% (p150), while AAR Canadian carloads in mid-July were +1.9% (p190); net a near-flat to slightly-down July 2026 is the central case, with a wide range reflecting wildfire disruption and grain-program uncertainty.
assumptions.applies_when: July 2026 total tonnage is close to July 2025 with modest YoY drift.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a large grain-program surge or a major multi-week mainline closure in July 2026.

assessment.note: Both from the same StatCan July 2025 release: p1 is the July 2025 level (30.7 Mt) and p2 the five-year July average (29.8 Mt); they are consistent and establish that July 2025 was slightly above its seasonal norm. Same underlying survey, so not independent confirmation.

Decomposition of the July 2025 total: non-intermodal 24.2 Mt (p5) + intermodal 3.2 Mt (p7) + US-connection loadings 3.3 Mt (p3) ≈ 30.7 Mt (p1); p12 (10.8% US share) is consistent with 3.3/30.7. All from the same StatCan release, so internally consistent by construction rather than independent.
Repeated statements of the same 12.0% average US-connection share for 2023-2024 across StatCan and AgCanada copies; one underlying measurement, redundant copies.
Quarterly/monthly US-share path in 2025 (11.3% Jan, 10.2% Feb, 10.3% Mar, 10.7% Q1, 10.5% Q2, 10.8% Jul) — same series, shows the US-connection share drifting down from the 12% 2023-24 norm.

CEIC mirrors of StatCan carloadings for 1999-2020 (levels, averages, highs/lows, commodity detail). Same underlying survey, older vintage; useful only as long-run context and for the pre-2020 level, not for the July 2026 level.

November 2024 StatCan release: total 30.8 Mt (p295) vs five-year November average 31.3 Mt (p296), with component detail (domestic non-intermodal 25.2, intermodal 2.5, US 3.2). Same survey, different month; shows the ~30-31 Mt monthly plateau and the component structure.

March 2025 StatCan release: total 33.3 Mt (p310) vs five-year March average 32.8 Mt (p312), Q1 2025 cumulative 92.3 Mt (p313). Same survey; establishes the seasonal high in Q1 and the ~30-33 Mt monthly range.

February 2026 StatCan release: total 29.4 Mt (p250), +9.8% y/y (p251), below the February record 30.7 Mt (p252); components 23.2 non-intermodal, 3.0 intermodal, 3.2 US. This is the most recent target-adjacent evidence and shows 2026 running above 2025 in the winter months, with potash and canola strong and iron/steel weak.
December 2025 StatCan release (duplicated across several ids): total 31.0 Mt, non-intermodal 24.8, intermodal 2.8, US 3.3. Same survey; confirms the ~31 Mt level at end-2025.
Annual totals: 2025 = 376.6 Mt, 2024 = 377.3 Mt (duplicated ids). Same survey; implies a monthly mean of ~31.4 Mt and near-flat y/y growth in 2025.

Annual 2025 commodity loadings (wheat 31.1 Mt, other cereals 7.8, coal 38.5, canola 8.8, fuel oils 10.0, lumber 7.3). Same survey; gives commodity scale for a sum-of-components check but no July 2026 detail.

CN weekly operating metrics for late July / week ending Aug 1 2026: carloads 100,390 (p147), RTMs 4,287 (p148), carloads -4.1% y/y (p149), RTMs -2.3% y/y (p150). Single-carrier, weekly; a near-real-time proxy for July 2026 volume direction, not the StatCan total.

AAR weekly for week ending July 11 2026: Canadian carloads 89,784 (p190), intermodal 73,506 (p191), cumulative 27-week total 4,440,435 (p192); US and Mexican comparators. AAR is a different compiler from StatCan but draws on the same carriers' reports; useful as a July 2026 activity cross-check, not a tonnage measure.

Ag Transport Coalition hopper-car fulfillment data for the 2026-27 crop year (weeks 1-2, ~Aug 2026) and week 37-38 2025-26: system fulfillment 88-90%, CN weaker (79%) than CPKC (99%). Indicates grain logistics were functioning but CN-constrained in early crop year 2026-27; relevant to July grain movement only indirectly (July is pre-harvest).

Wildfire disruption near Armstrong/Thunder Bay in July 2026 (p174: CN crew halted July 13 2026; p169: 315,431 ha fire; p173: 6 communities evacuated). Qualitative shock evidence; no quantified closure days, so cannot be converted to tonnage without an assumption.

Apparent tension: July 2025 was 30.7 Mt and down 0.4% y/y, while February 2026 was +9.8% y/y. Not a true contradiction — different months and a genuine 2026 upswing in winter bulk (potash, canola) — but it means a flat y/y July 2026 assumption is not obviously right; the 2026 trend is positive.

a1.role: Ratio of July 2026 total tonnage to July 2025 total tonnage

methods.rationale: Reuses the round-1 anchor route: July 2025 total (p1) scaled by a July 2026/July 2025 change factor. The factor is informed by the 2026 winter upswing (p251), CN's late-July 2026 carload/RTM declines (p149, p150), and the wildfire disruption (p174). Shared dependency: p1 is the same StatCan survey as the target; the factor is the only free parameter and carries the main uncertainty.

methods.rationale: Sum-of-components route: the July 2025 total decomposes into non-intermodal (p5), intermodal (p7) and US-connection loadings (p3), each scaled by a segment-specific change factor. This is a different structural route from m1 (it uses the component split rather than the total), though it shares the same StatCan survey and the same July 2025 base year. Failure mode: the three components may not be exactly exhaustive/additive in StatCan's definitions, and the segment factors are assumption-driven.

assumptions.name: July 2026 vs July 2025 total tonnage change factor
assumptions.rationale: July 2025 was 30.7 Mt, slightly above the five-year July average of 29.8 Mt (p1, p2). 2026 has run above 2025 in winter (February 2026 +9.8% y/y, p251), but CN's late-July 2026 carloads were -4.1% y/y and RTMs -2.3% y/y (p149, p150), and July 2026 had wildfire disruption near Armstrong/Thunder Bay (p174). These pull in opposite directions, so the central factor is 1.0 with a wide range spanning a modest decline to a modest gain.
assumptions.applies_when: The July 2026 StatCan total is driven mainly by the same commodity mix and carrier network as July 2025, with no major strike or port closure lasting most of the month.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a multi-week CN/CPKC mainline closure, a Vancouver/Prince Rupert port strike, or a grain/potash program collapse in July 2026 that would push the factor well below 0.94.

assumptions.name: July 2026 vs July 2025 non-intermodal commodity tonnage change factor
assumptions.rationale: Non-intermodal (bulk commodity) traffic was 24.2 Mt in July 2025 (p5) and 23.2 Mt in February 2026, up 8.3% y/y (p253, p254). Potash and canola were strong in early 2026 (p262, p263) while iron/steel was weak (p264). July is pre-harvest, so grain is carryover-driven; the net factor is centred at 1.0 with a wide range.
assumptions.applies_when: Bulk commodity flows in July 2026 follow the early-2026 pattern of strong potash/canola offset by weak metals, with no major mine or elevator outage.
assumptions.falsified_by: A documented collapse in potash exports or a grain-elevator strike in July 2026.

assumptions.name: July 2026 vs July 2025 intermodal tonnage change factor
assumptions.rationale: Intermodal was 3.2 Mt in July 2025, up 9.4% y/y (p7), and 3.0 Mt in February 2026, up 15% y/y (p255, p256). Container traffic has been the strongest-growing segment; a modest further gain in July 2026 is plausible, tempered by US tariff effects on transborder containers.
assumptions.applies_when: Container volumes continue the 2025-26 growth trend without a port or terminal disruption.
assumptions.falsified_by: A sharp drop in container throughput at Vancouver/Prince Rupert or a rail intermodal terminal closure in July 2026.

assumptions.name: July 2026 vs July 2025 US-connection tonnage change factor
assumptions.rationale: US-connection loadings were 3.3 Mt in July 2025, down 19.2% y/y (p3, p4), and 3.2 Mt in February 2026 (p257), with the US share drifting from 12% (2023-24) to ~10.4% in 2025 (p260). The downward trend suggests a slight further decline, but the range is wide given tariff uncertainty.
assumptions.applies_when: US transborder traffic continues its post-2024 decline without a new tariff shock or recovery.
assumptions.falsified_by: A rebound in US-connection loadings reported for mid-2026 or a new tariff regime sharply cutting transborder volumes.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
